lesson_title: A Town That Breathes: Business Cycles
hook_text: One mine's siren sets the rhythm for every till in town. That rhythm has a name.
clip_script: Picture a platinum-belt mining town. The metal price has been low for two years: skeleton shifts, empty hostel beds, the hardware store dusting shelves it hasn't restocked. Nothing getting worse — just flat. That's the TROUGH. Then the price lifts. The mine recalls a shift, the contractor hires welders, pay-day queues return to the ATMs. Those wages hit the taxi rank and the shisanyama, and those takings get spent again — the town climbs month by month. UPSWING. Then it maxes out: overtime on every roster, not a spare boilermaker at any wage, rents jumping every renewal. PEAK — the town cannot produce more, so prices climb instead. Then the price turns. Overtime cancelled, then a shift. The welder's wages vanish from the till, the furniture shop stops ordering, each loss knocks over the next. DOWNSWING — until it flattens into a new trough. That is a business cycle: trough, upswing, peak, downswing, riding a slow upward slope called the trend. And somebody leans against the wave: the Reserve Bank dialled the repo rate down in 2020 to heat a frozen economy, and up in 2022 to cool a fevered one. Not to punish you. To keep the town breathing steadily.
visual_style: One dusty mining-town main road cycling through boom and bust in continuous time-lapse: headgear wheels stopping and spinning, ATM queues growing and thinning, scaffolding rising, shutters closing — while a wave-line traces the town's pulse above the rooftops.
mood: Grounded and observational, sharpening into clarity.
pacing: Still at the trough, accelerating through the upswing, a held beat at the peak, tumbling through the downswing, steady close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and name any economy's phase — and the policy answer — in one line.
